MECHANICAL-BIRD RELEASE — releasing a brass mechanical messenger-bird from its cage on the signal-deck, the bird already mid-wing-beat and lifting from her open palm, gears and rotors whirring audibly, her other hand still holding the cage door open, slipstream immediately catching the bird's vaned wings, the recipient airship's navigation-lights blinking two miles ahead in the darkening sky.

VORTEX BOW-STANDING — standing on the bow-platform mid-vortex with coat fully horizontal behind her like a wing, both hands gripping the bowsprit-rails, body leaning forward into the rotational wind, hair whipping in tight opposing arcs from the conflicting air-currents, the vortex wall curving up on both sides of the hull, the far eye of the system visible directly ahead and closing.

COURSE-PLOT CHART GAUGES — plotting a new evasion-course on the chart-table with a brass quill, the quill mid-stroke across the chart, her other elbow pinning the chart flat against the slipstream coming through the open bridge-window, amber gauges glowing in a row behind her head, a second officer's hand pointing urgently at a position two inches ahead of the quill's current line.

BRIDGE COMMAND — Shouting course-corrections through a brass speaking-tube while leaning hard over the chart-table on the bridge, brass quill still clutched in her free hand, gas-lit gauges flaring amber behind her, brass dividers skidding across the chart in the slipstream, the helmsman already spinning the wheel hard.

FUSE-LIGHTING — Crouching at the cannon-port with a brass match-striker flaring in her fist, lighting the fuse mid-motion, the trailing spark already racing toward the powder-charge, her shoulder pressed against the hot cannon-breech, smoke stinging her squinting eye, the enemy ship's silhouette filling the port beyond.

RIGGING REPAIR — Climbing the dirigible-rigging mid-storm to patch a shredding fin, brass-handled wrench gripped between her teeth, rope looped around her gauntleted forearm, lightning forking past the dirigible-spine a yard behind her, hair ripped completely loose and streaming horizontal, the torn canvas panel whipping inches from her face.

CUTLASS PARRY — Parrying a sky-cutlass blow on the gunwale, sparks showering from the locked blades, her back heel braced against the brass railing, free hand driving her elbow into the enemy boarder's chest, the second attacker visible mid-swing behind the first, both coat-sleeves billowing from the force of impact.

SPYGLASS SWEEP — Leaning into the slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, brass spyglass extended and pressed hard to her eye, body angled sharply against the wind, coat-tails streaming fully horizontal, the ship-deck a narrow plank far below, an enemy sail-shape materializing in the cloud-gap at the lens's edge.

RIGGING SWING — Swinging on a rigging-line between two airships mid-dogfight, both brass pistols leveled and firing, muzzle-flash from each barrel simultaneously, spent shells tumbling into open sky below, coat billowing into a full wing-shape, hair horizontal in the gap-wind, the enemy deck rushing up to meet her boots.

WHEEL-AND-GLASS — Gripping the helm-wheel with her left hand while driving the ship hard into a bank, brass spyglass raised in her right, body angled against the heel, gauges swinging wildly on the bridge panel behind her, the enemy ship crossing into her spyglass frame just as the deck tilts further.

FLARE-PISTOL SIGNAL — Firing a signal-flare from a brass-handled pistol off the prow-railing, the flare already arcing upward trailing red smoke, recoil snapping her wrist back, coat surging in the bow-wind, hair whipping across her shoulder, the answering ship still dark in the cloud below, no reply-flare yet visible.

SPAR SPRINT — Sprinting along the top-spar with sky-cutlass raised, boots hitting the narrow beam mid-stride, coat tearing sideways in the open-air slipstream, hair streaming back in a solid rope, the enemy boarding-ramp clanging down onto the spar ahead, the first enemy figure already stepping onto the beam toward her.
